\chapter{The correspondence with the C code}\label{chap:correspondence}

The model is checked against ratpoints v3.1.1 (commit \texttt{1a998538dfa8}). The C files below are those of the library and \texttt{main.c}, whose parts that the command-line program does not mirror are to be excluded. Every line of code of them lies in at most one recorded range: a range is either modelled by the Lean declarations named, or excluded from the model with a reason. Each recorded range is checked against the text it had when it was reviewed.

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.barrett}: natural numbers for the \texttt{unsigned long}s, the product \texttt{u m} exact as the 128-bit product of the C code, and the difference exact, which does not wrap since the quotient times \texttt{p} is at most \texttt{u} for \texttt{m ≤ (2 \textasciicircum{} 64 -{} 1) / p}; the obligation that \texttt{u} is below \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 64}, which the C type gives, a hypothesis of the lemma that the result is \texttt{u \% p}; the form with the 128-bit product, which the builds of the model compile (the compiler defines \texttt{\_\_SIZEOF\_INT128\_\_}, and \texttt{RP\_NO\_INT128} is not set), for the division \texttt{u \% p} of the other builds, which gives the same remainder.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{1652}{1655}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.hornerSteps}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.hornerSteps}: computed from \texttt{Ratpoints.maxBitsInPrime} as the macro computes it from \texttt{RATPOINTS\_MAX\_BITS\_IN\_PRIME}, with \texttt{64} for \texttt{LONG\_LENGTH}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{1683}{1697}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}: the prime \texttt{p} itself, for its index \texttt{pn} in the table \texttt{prime}; the table a fresh array of \texttt{p + 1} entries, for the integers that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer \texttt{int\_next} and hands back through \texttt{is\_f\_square\_p}, and the coefficients a fresh array returned with the entry, for the array \texttt{coeffs\_mod\_p} of its caller, which it fills; one loop over the residues, for the two loops of the two branches of the schedule of Horner's rule, between which \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.hornerBarrett} chooses for each residue; the residues with a square value are not counted, and the exit asks only whether one entry is true, which is the test on the count \texttt{np} and the entry \texttt{p}; the entry is made also when \texttt{f(a)} is a square for every residue and there is no point at infinity modulo \texttt{p}, where \texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, the moduli being an input of the model, and for both of its codes \texttt{1} and \texttt{2}, which only the choice of the moduli tells apart, with the density and the fields of \texttt{prec\_entry} (stage I); the entry is a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and returned, where \texttt{examine\_prime} stores it in the field \texttt{ssp} of \texttt{prec\_entry}; it keeps only \texttt{p}, the table and the inverses (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry}), and no rows: those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.rows}) are made from it when they are first needed, also the row of \texttt{0}, which \texttt{examine\_prime} installs from the build; the fields \texttt{init}, \texttt{nf} and \texttt{pw} that \texttt{examine\_prime} sets (lines 1800 and 1817) are those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}), of which the prime is the single factor, made by \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}; no reciprocal \texttt{magic}, bias \texttt{bias} and inverse \texttt{rbainv}, which serve the reduction of the sieve and the packing (stage F).)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.siftPiece}: a fresh array of zeros for each piece, for the survivors array of the sieving thread, which every piece reuses, with one bit array more for the alignment, and whose words \texttt{malloc} leaves uninitialized; the piece by its first word number \texttt{w0} and its number \texttt{n} of bit arrays, for \texttt{w\_low} and \texttt{w\_high}, and an index for the pointer to its last bit array; the moduli of all three stages with their rows in \texttt{specs}, for the moduli of the first two stages with their rows in \texttt{sieves}, the numbers \texttt{sp1}, \texttt{sp2} and \texttt{nchecks} of the moduli of the stages, which the sieving thread \texttt{wk} keeps, and the table \texttt{checks} of the third stage (stage F); the class word \texttt{cw}, the pattern \texttt{bits} of the class \texttt{cls} (\texttt{sift.c:519}) at the stride 1, for the class itself, whose stride \texttt{k} and residue \texttt{a0}, which the extraction reads (\texttt{sift.c:1221-{}1222}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}; \texttt{sift.c:1130-{}1131} under \texttt{USE\_LONG\_IN\_PHASE\_2}), come with the packing (stage F); no \texttt{magics} and no test \texttt{small} of whether the reductions modulo the moduli can multiply by a reciprocal (stage F); no count of the words of the piece (\texttt{n\_words}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I); the products \texttt{w} and the factor \texttt{f} of the check as arguments, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} computes the products when the first survivor of \texttt{b} reaches it and multiplies each value by \texttt{b} for odd \texttt{d}; a list of points, for the callback \texttt{process} with its argument \texttt{info} and for the count \texttt{total} of points that \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} returns, with no flag \texttt{quit} for a stop that \texttt{process} may request (stage G); natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s (stage F); no measurements of the phases (\texttt{RP\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_TOC}, \texttt{RP\_PHASE\_TIMING}) and no stop after one of them (\texttt{RP\_STOP\_AFTER}).)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{3149}{3170}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}: the plain layout, bit \texttt{t} of the bit array with the word number \texttt{w} for the numerator \texttt{rbaLength w + t}, and every numerator from \texttt{-{}H} to \texttt{H}, as the bits from \texttt{-{}H} to \texttt{H}, for the intervals of the search region that the Sturm step keeps (stage H), whose numerators ratpoints takes into the packing of the 2-adic class of \texttt{b} (\texttt{interval\_bits}, \texttt{numerators\_to\_bits}; stage F), returning at the first interval beyond \texttt{H} and skipping an empty one; the class word \texttt{cw} of \texttt{b}, the pattern of its class at the stride 1, for the class \texttt{cls} itself, whose stride \texttt{k} and residue \texttt{a0} (read through \texttt{interval\_bits} by \texttt{numerators\_to\_bits}) and row offsets (read by \texttt{set\_rows}) come with the packing (stage F); the row of \texttt{b mod p}, read in \texttt{sift} from the rows of the run and made by its thunk when it is first needed, for the row of \texttt{b 2\textasciicircum{}(-{}k) mod p} that \texttt{set\_rows} reads from the residues that \texttt{fill\_bp\_list} computes before the call (stage F), with a test for the rows that are missing and their construction by the function \texttt{init} of the entry under the lock of the tables, which threads share; every modulus with its row, those of the third stage too, for the moduli of the first two stages with their rows, the offset of the packing and the end of the row (\texttt{sieve\_spec}), and the table \texttt{checks} of the third stage, which \texttt{fill\_checks} fills when the first numerator of \texttt{b} reaches that stage, with the inverse of \texttt{b} modulo each of its moduli, from \texttt{b mod p} by a multiplication when \texttt{b} is small, and the magic and the bias of the reductions (stage F); the products \texttt{w} and the factor \texttt{f} computed for every denominator, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} computes the products when the first survivor of \texttt{b} reaches it (\texttt{compute\_bc}) and multiplies each value by \texttt{b} for odd \texttt{d}; no count of the denominators sieved (\texttt{n\_sifts}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I), and no flag \texttt{stage3\_filled} (stage F); a list of points, for the callback \texttt{process} with its argument \texttt{info} and for the count \texttt{total} of points that \texttt{sift} returns, with no stop that \texttt{process} may request (\texttt{quit}, stage G) or that the pool of threads sends (\texttt{stop}); natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s (stage F); no measurements of the phases (\texttt{RP\_SIFT\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_SETUP\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_INIT\_TIC} and their \texttt{TOC}) and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4523}{4528}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), for the codes and the order of the library: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height}, so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses, and with no bound \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63 -{} 1}, which only the program's reading of the height imposes (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}). A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller (the reversed coefficients, the degree, the flags), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the points are returned as a list, for the count \texttt{total} and the flag \texttt{quit} of the callback (stage G); the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it, is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set. No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4542}{4545}: excluded (interface): the input fields of the arguments that find\_points\_work saves, so that a caller who reuses the arguments for the next curve does not find the normalizations and choices of the search in them; the model writes nothing back
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4546}{4546}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), for the codes and the order of the library: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height}, so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses, and with no bound \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63 -{} 1}, which only the program's reading of the height imposes (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}). A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller (the reversed coefficients, the degree, the flags), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the points are returned as a list, for the count \texttt{total} and the flag \texttt{quit} of the callback (stage G); the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it, is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set. No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4573}{4573}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}: the arguments of \texttt{sieving\_info} that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the 2-adic classes and the word \texttt{den\_bits}) are not modelled; the denominators from \texttt{1} to \texttt{H}, for the range \texttt{b\_low, …, b\_high} (stage H); the flags of the denominators as Booleans, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the forbidden divisors and the divisors of the leading coefficient with their records as lists, for the arrays \texttt{args-{}>forb\_ba}, \texttt{args-{}>forbidden}, \texttt{args-{}>den\_info} and \texttt{args-{}>divisors} of the arguments; the square test \texttt{lcfsq} of line 4906 made on the polynomial searched (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.isSquare}), where the C code computes it before the reversal check (line 4634) and clears it in case 2 (line 4770): the same value for an even degree, the only one that reads it; the test on \texttt{point\_at\_infty} of the 2-adic exit recomputed, as \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} decides it; the exits give the empty list, where \texttt{sieving\_info} returns the prime and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} the number \texttt{0} of points found; the Sturm step does not restrict the search region before stage H, so that the return when it leaves nothing to search is never taken, and the run always follows the points at infinity; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4643}{4649}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve (\texttt{sieving\_info}), looks past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent and the curve needs it, chooses the cut points from the curve when \texttt{-{}n} or \texttt{-{}N} is absent or negative, and corrects the choice during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}); the third stage is the rest of the list after \texttt{s₂}, where ratpoints takes up to \texttt{P} primes after \texttt{s₂}, or primes up to all \texttt{Ratpoints.numPrimes} when \texttt{-{}P} is absent or negative, from those it has looked at, which are among the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is given (line 2980, \texttt{may\_extend = 0}); the model examines the primes of the third stage beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); the number \texttt{examined} of the primes examined, which stands for \texttt{pn\_lim} of \texttt{sieving\_info} (line 2566), is \texttt{q}, as in ratpoints when \texttt{-{}p} is given, where it looks at more primes when \texttt{-{}p} is absent and the choice of the moduli needs them.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), for the codes and the order of the library: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height}, so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses, and with no bound \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63 -{} 1}, which only the program's reading of the height imposes (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}). A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller (the reversed coefficients, the degree, the flags), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the points are returned as a list, for the count \texttt{total} and the flag \texttt{quit} of the callback (stage G); the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it, is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set. No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4894}{4899}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}: the flag \texttt{rev} as an argument, for the bit \texttt{RATPOINTS\_REVERSED} of the flags of the search (\texttt{args-{}>flags}); a list of points for the callback \texttt{process}, with no stop it may request, no \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_Y} and no \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} (stage G), and no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}; the square test of \texttt{c\_d} and the decision whether there are points at infinity are made on the list that it is given, after the reversal check, when the points are delivered, where the C code computes \texttt{lcfsq} before the check (line 4634), which clears it when it reverses a polynomial of even degree and leaves it, unread, with the odd degree of the other reversals, and sets \texttt{point\_at\_infty} before the exits of the search (lines 4894-4899); the case \texttt{c\_d = 0}, that of the zero polynomial, which ratpoints refuses before it gets here, gives the one point \texttt{(a, 0, b)}, which the cited lines, delivering \texttt{-{}y} without a test \texttt{y ≠ 0}, would deliver twice.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4900}{4943}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}: the arguments of \texttt{sieving\_info} that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the 2-adic classes and the word \texttt{den\_bits}) are not modelled; the denominators from \texttt{1} to \texttt{H}, for the range \texttt{b\_low, …, b\_high} (stage H); the flags of the denominators as Booleans, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the forbidden divisors and the divisors of the leading coefficient with their records as lists, for the arrays \texttt{args-{}>forb\_ba}, \texttt{args-{}>forbidden}, \texttt{args-{}>den\_info} and \texttt{args-{}>divisors} of the arguments; the square test \texttt{lcfsq} of line 4906 made on the polynomial searched (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.isSquare}), where the C code computes it before the reversal check (line 4634) and clears it in case 2 (line 4770): the same value for an even degree, the only one that reads it; the test on \texttt{point\_at\_infty} of the 2-adic exit recomputed, as \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} decides it; the exits give the empty list, where \texttt{sieving\_info} returns the prime and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} the number \texttt{0} of points found; the Sturm step does not restrict the search region before stage H, so that the return when it leaves nothing to search is never taken, and the run always follows the points at infinity; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{5219}{5220}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPoints}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), for the codes and the order of the library: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height}, so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses, and with no bound \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63 -{} 1}, which only the program's reading of the height imposes (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}). A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller (the reversed coefficients, the degree, the flags), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the points are returned as a list, for the count \texttt{total} and the flag \texttt{quit} of the callback (stage G); the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it, is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set. No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)

the products \texttt{w} and the factor \texttt{f} computed for every denominator, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} computes the products when the first survivor of \texttt{b} reaches it (\texttt{compute\_bc}) and multiplies each value by \texttt{b} for odd \texttt{d}; no count of the denominators sieved (\texttt{n\_sifts}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I), and no flag \texttt{stage3\_filled} (stage F); a list of points, for the callback \texttt{process} with its argument \texttt{info} and for the count \texttt{total} of points that \texttt{sift} returns, with no stop that \texttt{process} may request (\texttt{quit}, stage G) or that the pool of threads sends (\texttt{stop}); \begin{itemize}

\item \csource{init.c}{42}{46}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry.admits}, \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.row}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry.admits}: the bit of \texttt{a} in the row of \texttt{r}, computed from the tables for each numerator, where ratpoints builds the row of a residue \texttt{r ≠ 0} once, when a denominator first needs it, as a bit pattern of \texttt{p} bits repeated through words, by a function for each prime that the build generates, and takes the row of \texttt{0} from the pattern \texttt{sieves0} that the build generates, whose bit \texttt{N} is clear exactly when \texttt{p} divides \texttt{N}.)
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.row}: one function for every kind of modulus, the pattern of one period from \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.admits} laid out in words by windows into its packed form, as \texttt{lay\_out\_pattern} lays out the pattern of a prime power, for the builders of the rows of a prime in \texttt{init.c}, which step through the residues \texttt{a b⁻¹ mod p} four at a time and rotate the pattern through the words, one function for each prime that the build generates, for the pattern \texttt{sieves0} that the build generates for the row of \texttt{0} of a prime, and for the row of a product, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sieve\_init\_product} lays down from the rows of its factors (stage F); in \texttt{lay\_out\_pattern}, the packed pattern made bit by bit, where it is or-ed together from shifted copies of the pattern, the position of each window computed, where it is stepped by \texttt{64 mod p}, and the first \texttt{p} words repeated, where all \texttt{p rbaPack} are computed; a fresh array, for the space that the builders take from the buffer of the tables (\texttt{ba\_next}), and the row returned, where the builders also store it in the field \texttt{sieve} of the entry, with a release store for the threads (\texttt{RP\_PUBLISH}), which the thunks of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.rows} do; the copies of the first bit arrays that the builders append at the end of a row, which only the chunked first stage reads, are none in the build of the model (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHUNK} = 1; stage F).)

\section*{\texttt{sturm.c}}
\begin{itemize}
\item \csource{sturm.c}{29}{97}: not yet recorded (29 lines of code)
\item \csource{sturm.c}{99}{163}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.chain}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sturm.chain}: the rows as arrays of their coefficients up to their degree, for the table of \texttt{(d + 1)\textasciicircum{}2} GMP integers and the array of degrees, with no \texttt{mpz\_init} and \texttt{mpz\_clear} (a chain has at most \texttt{d + 1} rows, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.IsChain.size\_le}, and its row \texttt{k + 1} at most \texttt{d -{} k} entries, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sturm.IsChain.size\_getElem!\_add\_one\_add\_le}): an array has one entry more than the degree of its row, and a remainder that becomes zero is the empty array, where the degree in the C code reaches \texttt{-{}1}; a reduction step drops the leading coefficient, which it makes \texttt{0}, where the C code lowers the degree; the rows are handed back, and \texttt{none} for the return of \texttt{-{}1}, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_compute\_sturm} keeps them in its table for the rest of the Sturm step (stage H), and the index of the last row, which the C code leaves in \texttt{k} and sets to \texttt{d} after the loop for \texttt{d = 1}, is the size of the array less one; a list of integers for the array of GMP integers of the coefficients, local values for the scratch integers \texttt{work[0]}, \texttt{work[1]} and \texttt{work[2]}, and Lean's \texttt{/} for \texttt{mpz\_fdiv\_q}, which agree on the divisions of the chain, all exact.)
\item \csource{sturm.c}{166}{332}: not yet recorded (136 lines of code)
\end{itemize}

\item \csource{rp-private.h}{170}{170}: excluded (other): the include of the vector intrinsics in the build USE\_AVX, with 256-bit bit arrays; the word operations of the model need none
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{172}{173}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaLength}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaLength}: computed from \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack}, where each build sets \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH} and its logarithm \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} by literals; the shifts by \texttt{RBA\_SHIFT} and by \texttt{LONG\_SHIFT} are divisions by \texttt{rbaLength} and by 64, and the masks by \texttt{RBA\_LENGTH -{} 1} and by \texttt{LONG\_MASK} remainders.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{174}{175}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.rbaPack}: the value of the default build, set here, where the C code chooses the build by the macros that the compiler is given; the vector type of a bit array becomes \texttt{rbaPack} consecutive words of an array of \texttt{UInt64}.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{176}{176}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andBitArray}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andBitArray}: one definition for every build, on bit arrays given by their indices in arrays of words, each bit array \texttt{rbaPack} consecutive words, for the \texttt{\&} on the vector type of the build.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{177}{178}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}: the plain layout, bit \texttt{t} of the bit array with the word number \texttt{w} for the numerator \texttt{rbaLength w + t}, where bit \texttt{t} stands for the numerator \texttt{a₀ + 2\textasciicircum{}k (rbaLength w + t)} of the packing of the 2-adic class of \texttt{b} (stage F); indices for the pointers into the survivors, and a scan that holds its position as an index and reads the words of the bit array that it finds in place, where ratpoints recovers the word number from a pointer difference and copies the bit array; the sentinel \texttt{\textasciitilde{}zero} of every build as \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack} words \texttt{\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}0}, written one at a time, and the reads \texttt{EXT0} and \texttt{EXT} as words of the array, for the vector type of the build, with one loop over the words of a bit array for the read of the first word and the loop over the others; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s (stage F); no count of the bit arrays that survive the first stage (\texttt{n\_arrays}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I).)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{179}{202}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.isZeroAt}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.isZeroAt}: one definition for every build, on a bit array given by its index in an array of words, \texttt{rbaPack} consecutive words that it compares with \texttt{0} one at a time, for the tests of the builds on the vector type, with vector instructions or by or-ing its words; the test for zero \texttt{TESTZ} also stands for its negation \texttt{TEST}.)
\item \csource{rp-private.h}{203}{204}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andRows}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.andRows}: every modulus in the first stage, over every bit array, for the second stage, which and-s the rows of its moduli, one after the other, into each bit array that the scan finds nonzero, and stops as soon as no bit of it is left, and the third stage, which tests one numerator at a time after the test for common factors, stops at the first prime that rejects it and skips the primes that divide \texttt{b} (stage F); the first stage of the builds with one register per chunk, for the chunks of sixteen registers of the default build with the legs over the tail of a piece (stage F); the class word written one word at a time from the first, where ratpoints writes the 2-adic pattern of the class of \texttt{b} into the bit arrays from the last, and the pattern of the plain layout, one word repeated, for the packed pattern of a stride \texttt{2\textasciicircum{}k} (stage F), the class word written into each word of a bit array, for the vector \texttt{RBA(packed)} that \texttt{get\_2adic\_info} makes once per class (\texttt{find\_points.c:1098}) and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} copies into each bit array (\texttt{bits64}, \texttt{sift.c:519}, \texttt{sift.c:954}); the row of the word number \texttt{w} at index \texttt{w mod p}, where ratpoints adds the offset of the packing and a multiple of \texttt{p} that keeps the index non-negative, and reduces by a multiplication when that is exact (stage F); indices for the pointers into the rows and into the survivors, and the number of whole periods and the rest computed before their loops; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s (stage F); no count of the ands of the second stage under \texttt{RP\_PHASE\_COUNTS}, and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve (\texttt{sieving\_info}), looks past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent and the curve needs it, chooses the cut points from the curve when \texttt{-{}n} or \texttt{-{}N} is absent or negative, and corrects the choice during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}); the third stage is the rest of the list after \texttt{s₂}, where ratpoints takes up to \texttt{P} primes after \texttt{s₂}, or primes up to all \texttt{Ratpoints.numPrimes} when \texttt{-{}P} is absent or negative, from those it has looked at, which are among the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is given (line 2980, \texttt{may\_extend = 0}); the model examines the primes of the third stage beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); the number \texttt{examined} of the primes examined, which stands for \texttt{pn\_lim} of \texttt{sieving\_info} (line 2566), is \texttt{q}, as in ratpoints when \texttt{-{}p} is given, where it looks at more primes when \texttt{-{}p} is absent and the choice of the moduli needs them.)
